q: What type of butt hinge is ideal for heavy doors?
n: Ball-bearing butt hinges carry heavy, high-traffic doors with less wear and friction. Plain-bearing hinges are for light doors. Source: ANSI/BHMA A156.1 (Butts and Hinges); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated, Ch. 8.

q: What type of hinge is installed in two mortises between the jamb and door leaf?
n: Invisible (concealed, e.g. SOSS-type) hinges are mortised into both the jamb and the door edge. They are hidden when the door is closed. Source: ANSI/BHMA A156.26 (Continuous and Concealed Hinges); hardware manufacturers' data.

q: What type of hinge is used to install heavy metal gates?
n: Heavy metal gates hang on welded barrel (bullet) hinges, which carry large loads on a pin. Source: Gate hardware references; ANSI/BHMA A156.1.

q: Inset, full overlay and half-overlay are types of which hinge?
n: Concealed cabinet (cup) hinges come in full-overlay, half-overlay and inset versions, according to how the door sits on the carcass. Source: Architectural Woodwork Standards (AWI); hinge manufacturers' catalogs.

q: What is the standard diameter of cup holes?
n: Cup holes are used to install cabinet hinges. Concealed cabinet hinges fit a standard 35 mm cup hole bored into the door. Source: Hinge manufacturers' technical data (35 mm cup standard); Architectural Woodwork Standards.

q: What is the approximate total weight in kg of a W12x36 steel beam 6m long?
n: The designation of a wide flange beam is W(depth) x (unit weight in lbs/ft). Let’?s convert lbs/ft into kg/m. Remember that 1kg = 2.2lbs and 1m = 3.3ft. Therefore, the unit weight is around 54kg/m. Since the beam is 6m, the weight of the wide flange beam is 324kg. W12×36 weighs 36 lb/ft (about 53.6 kg/m). For 6 m: 53.6 × 6 ≈ 321 kg, or roughly 324 kg. Source: AISC Steel Construction Manual, Table 1-1 (W-Shapes).

q: If the project owner decides to put up a 10-room motel structure in the area, how many parking slots would not be enough?
n: See the parking provisions on Table 7.4 of the NBCP for motels, It says there, 1:1 parking provisions shall be considered for motels. Therefore, the minimum shall be 10 units. NBC Table VII.4 requires one parking slot per motel room, so 10 rooms need 10 slots. 9 slots would not be enough. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VII, Table VII.4 (Parking – Motels).

q: What is the standard moisture content of wood ideal for construction?
n: Construction lumber should be dried to 19% moisture content or less. That is the "dry" grade, which limits shrinkage, warping and decay. Source: USDA Forest Products Laboratory, Wood Handbook, Ch. 4; NSCP 2015, Ch. 6 (Wood).

q: There are 12 boxes of 30cm x 30cm ceramic tiles on site. How much floor area can be covered by these boxes?
n: As a rule of thumb, a box of 30cm x 30cm of ceramic tiles can cover 1 sqm. Therefore, the approximate area that 12 boxes can cover is 12sqm. A box of 30 cm × 30 cm tiles usually holds 11 pieces, about 1 sqm. 12 boxes cover about 12 sqm. Source: Max Fajardo, Simplified Construction Estimate (Tiles); local tile packaging.

q: What is the recommended minimum spacing of downspouts?
n: The recommended spacing of downspouts is between 6m to 15m. Downspouts are commonly spaced about 6 m to 15 m apart, depending on roof area and rainfall intensity. About 6 m is the recommended minimum spacing. Source: Revised National Plumbing Code (Storm Drainage – Rainwater Leaders); SMACNA Architectural Sheet Metal Manual.

q: For better indoor air quality, what should be the minimum distance of outdoor smoking areas from building openings?
n: Designated smoking areas must be in open spaces at least 10 m away from entrances, exits and air intakes. That keeps smoke out of the building. Source: Executive Order No. 26 (2017), Sec. 4 (Designated Smoking Areas); DOH implementing guidelines.

q: What is the footprint of the building?
n: The 60 m frontage on a 2,400 sqm lot gives a depth of 40 m. Subtract the 7 m front yard, 3 m rear yard and two 5 m side yards: 50 m x 30 m = 1,500 sqm. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VII, Sec. 707 (Building Footprint) and Rule VIII, Sec. 804 (Setbacks).
scenario:
DESIGN PROBLEM NO. 1 – SEVEN-STOREY GOVERNMENT OFFICE

Design Problem: The Local Government of Quezon City is planning to add a seven-storey civic center building in its City Hall Compound. This building will house several business departments catering the public. The city government allocates 2,400 sqm lot for this new building. The following spaces shall be accommodated in the planning:
a. The ground floor shall have a 25m x 30m covered parking on the SE side of the lot. This side of the building is where the exit discharge of the building is located. The exit discharge runs along the side yard of the lot to the public RROW. On the right side (when facing the lot), the lobby which measures 25m x 500sqm accommodates the waiting customers of the releasing office. The releasing office measuring 11m x 10m is located at the back of the building along the stairs, elevator and comfort rooms. The stairs and elevator have a combined area of 90sqm and located between the releasing office and the comfort room. The comfort room is measuring 5m wide and 10m long.
b. The comfort room, stairs and elevator areas are in the same size and location on the 2nd to 7th floor of the building. A 50m long and 2m wide corridor is running along the long side of the building. The comfort room, stair and elevator area is connected to this corridor. The corridor divides the floor into two offices - one large measuring 43m x 18m and one smaller office measuring 36m x 10m. A canteen is accessible on one end of the corridor which measures 7m x 126sqm. This layout is almost the same on the 3rd until 7th floor except that the areas of the canteen and large office are combined and divided equally. The 3rd to 7th floor has 3 offices - one measuring 360sqm and two measuring 450sqm. The rooftop of the building is not accessible to the public but can be used for mechanical and plumbing accessory rooms.
c. Half of the 7m-wide front yard shall be softscapes usable by the public. 10% of the parking shall have softscapes for better indoor air quality. Side setbacks measure 5m while rear setback is only 3m.
Site Features. The site is a regular lot fronting a road that connects East Avenue and Kalayaan Avenue. The road is named Makatarungan and has a 5m carriageway with 1.5m sidewalk on both sides. The longer front side of the lot is oriented 72° from North to West. This front side measures 60m. The slope of the lot is generally flat.
Design Objectives. Good circulation is a major consideration for the design since this is a public building. Within the offices, proper planning shall be done to accommodate the requirements of each office or department. Take note that each department has workflows which shall be the basis of the space plan. No waiting areas shall be located on the corridor. All waiting areas shall be within offices.

q: What is the area of the open space?
n: The TLA of the project is 2408 sqm. The footprint is 1500 sqm. Therefore, the open space (TOSL) is 900 sqm. Open space = lot area minus footprint = 2,400 sqm minus 1,500 sqm = 900 sqm. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VIII, Sec. 804 (Total Open Space within Lot).

q: What is the recommended parking slot size for parallel parking?
n: The NBC sets parallel parking slots at 2.15 m × 6.00 m. Perpendicular and angled slots are 2.50 m × 5.00 m. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VII, Sec. 707 (Parking slot dimensions).

q: What do you call the provision of an air gap between two layers of the building envelope?
n: Back ventilation is an open, ventilated air gap between the cladding and the inner wall. Air moving through the cavity carries away heat and moisture. Source: Straube & Burnett, Building Science for Building Enclosures (Ventilated Rainscreens).

q: The cold and dry wind usually appears from November to February. This wind pattern comes from which direction?
n: The Amihan (northeast monsoon) brings cool, dry air to the Philippines from about November to February. Source: PAGASA, Climate of the Philippines (Monsoons).

q: A native bahay-kubo structure is what type of construction?
n: The NBC classifies wood construction as Type I. A bahay kubo of bamboo, wood and nipa falls under it. Type V is fire-resistive construction. Source: PD 1096 (NBCP), Sec. 401 (Types of Construction).

q: Who shall sign the construction logbook submitted for certificate of occupancy?
n: Per the exam key, the construction logbook is signed by the B&C (builder/contractor) together with the full-time inspector/supervisor. It is then submitted with the application for occupancy. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule III (Certificate of Occupancy requirements).

q: How many elevators shall be installed in a single hoistway?
n: A single hoistway may hold no more than four elevator cars. Source: International Building Code, Sec. 3002.2 (Number of Elevator Cars in a Hoistway); ASME A17.1.

q: IFC drawings are also known as what?
n: IFC drawings are those drawing sets. which are issued by the design consultants or an Architect to the construction contractor. This term is not usually used for smaller projects. You can hear it in larger and more complex projects (i.e. international construction industries). IFC (Issued for Construction) drawings are the approved construction drawings released to the contractor for building. Source: Construction document practice; Architect's Guidelines (2016), Contract Documents Phase.

q: Which shall not precede the architectural design activity?
n: User identification, programming and space planning come before design. Outline specifications are prepared during or after schematic design, so they cannot precede it. Source: Architect's Guidelines (2016), Pre-Design and Schematic Design Phases.

q: In an office seating layout, staggered seating is ideal for what setting?
n: Staggered seating can be introduced in office seating layout to decrease the space between tables, which can be effective in tight areas. Staggered (offset) desk layouts shorten the distance between tables without facing users directly. That makes them effective in tight office areas. Source: Time-Saver Standards for Interior Design (Office Layouts); Panero & Zelnik, Human Dimension and Interior Space.

q: Which can describe adding two openings in a room to allow air circulation?
n: Cross ventilation uses openings on different walls, ideally opposite each other, so wind can flow through a room. Source: Lechner, Heating, Cooling, Lighting (Natural Ventilation); Koenigsberger et al., Manual of Tropical Housing and Building.

q: What is best introduced to a building design to facilitate stack ventilation?
n: An open central atrium is a tall shaft where warm air rises and exhausts at the top. It draws fresh air in at lower levels, which is the stack effect. Source: Lechner, Heating, Cooling, Lighting (Stack Ventilation); CIBSE AM10 (Natural Ventilation).

q: A zoning certificate can be requested from what agency?
n: Locational clearances and zoning certificates are issued by the zoning administrator, usually the City/Municipal Planning and Development Office. Source: HLURB Model Zoning Ordinance (Zoning Administration); Local Government Code (RA 7160).

q: In architectural documents, what should be the radius used for the vicinity map assuming a residential project?
n: A vicinity map shows the lot within a radius of about 500 m, enough to locate it relative to nearby streets and landmarks. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule III (Building Permit Requirements – Vicinity Map).

q: What is the maximum encroachment of foundation on public sidewalk?
n: Per the exam key, a footing may project at most 500 mm under a public sidewalk. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VIII and Rule X (Projection of Footings into Public Streets).

q: Written agreements imposing limitations on the use of property in a particular neighborhood.
n: Deed restrictions are written covenants in titles or sale contracts that limit how property in a neighborhood or subdivision may be used. Source: De Chiara & Koppelman, Time-Saver Standards for Site Planning; PD 957 (subdivision restrictions).

q: What do you call a coastal wetland where freshwater and ocean water mixes?
n: An estuary is the coastal water body where fresh river water mixes with seawater. Source: US EPA, National Estuary Program; Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction.

q: What type of furniture for the living area can be recommended?
n: For flexibility, a sectional sofa is more recommended. Sectional sofas can be rearranged into different configurations. That flexibility suits living areas of various sizes and layouts. Source: Ching, Interior Design Illustrated (Seating); Time-Saver Standards for Interior Design.

q: Xyladecor is used for what surface?
n: Xyladecor is Boysen’s product for wood staining. Xyladecor is a wood stain and preservative for timber surfaces. Source: Boysen (Pacific Paint) product data sheet; PDCA Painting Standards (Wood Stains).

q: Widened bottom steps in a staircase.
n: A curtail step is the widened bottom step of a stair, with a scroll-shaped end. Source: Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction (Curtail Step).

q: What is the safe variation of the stair tread and riser dimensions?
n: Within a flight, treads and risers may vary by no more than about 5 mm (3/16 in). Larger variations cause trips. Source: NFPA 101, Sec. 7.2.2.3.6 (Dimensional Uniformity); RA 9514 (Fire Code) RIRR.

q: What is the standard clearance below sprinkler heads?
n: A clear space of at least 450 mm (18 in) must be kept below sprinkler deflectors so the spray pattern develops. Source: NFPA 13, Sec. 8.5.6 (Clearance to Storage); RA 9514 RIRR.

q: What can describe an ottoman?
o: It is used in the dining area
It has neither backs nor arms
It is found in the foyer
It is placed against the wall
n: An ottoman is an upholstered seat or footstool with neither back nor arms. Source: Ching, Interior Design Illustrated (Furniture); Harris, Dictionary of Architecture and Construction.

q: It is the measure of lighting hitting a surface.
n: Illuminance, the light falling on a surface, is measured in lux (lumens per square meter). Candela is luminous intensity, and cd/m² is luminance. Source: IES Lighting Handbook (Photometric Quantities).

q: What type of luminaire is best for under-cabinet lighting?
n: Linear strip (LED tape or bar) luminaires fit under wall cabinets. They light the countertop evenly without glare. Source: IES Lighting Handbook (Residential Lighting – Task Lighting).

q: In a convenience store, an ACCU is usually placed where?
n: The air-cooled condensing unit rejects heat. In a convenience store it is placed outside, on the roof or an exterior ledge. Source: ASHRAE Handbook – Refrigeration (Retail Food Store Systems).

q: Which finishing material has the least embodied energy?
n: Of these four, brick has the least embodied energy (about 3 MJ/kg). Glass is about 15 MJ/kg, copper about 40 MJ/kg and aluminum about 155 MJ/kg. Source: Hammond & Jones, Inventory of Carbon and Energy (ICE), University of Bath.

q: What is the front setback used?
n: Per the exam key, a 5 m front setback was used for this commercial corner lot. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VIII, Sec. 804 and Table VIII.3 (Minimum Setbacks).

DESIGN PROBLEM NO. 5 – PROPOSED MEDIUM RISE COMMERCIAL BUILDING

Design Problem. A businesswoman commissioned you to design and construct a medium-rise commercial building in Pasig City. The building spaces will be rented to different kinds of establishments. After identifying the development controls and the user requirements, you came up with the following initial plan:
a. To maximize the profitability of the lot, you determined that the maximum building footprint allowed is 1,024sqm. No firewalls were introduced.
b. The building shall have the least number of storeys to be considered as medium- rise (according to the code). The GFA shall be 8,000sqm.
c. Underground parking shall be provided and the ground floor shall be reserved for a small supermarket or a fastfood chain. The upper floors shall accommodate other commercial establishments.
Site Features. The lot for this project is bounded on its two adjacent sides by roads - one with 20m width and the other with 15m width. The wider road runs along the east- west axis while the other runs along the north-south axis. The site measures 40m facing the wider road and has a total of 1,600sqm area. The north side of the lot is bounded by another undeveloped commercial lot while the west side is bounded by an existing commercial building with a maximized footprint (with firewall). The property slopes 2% downward towards the existing adjacent building. The area is zoned as medium intensity commercial area.
Design Objectives. Since the commercial building is open to any kind of establishments, you are challenged to create a building design and plans with flexibility in layout. The building facade shall also maximize its good orientation, having two frontages.

s: Design Problem 5 – Proposed Medium Rise Commercial Building
q: What is the side setback used?
n: Since it is a corner lot, the side and rear setbacks shall follow the largest setback provided by the code. From Table 8.2, it is determined that the minimum setback shall be 3m. A corner lot's side and rear yards follow the larger setback that the code requires for the zone. Here that is 3 m. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Rule VIII, Sec. 804 and Table VIII.3.

s: Design Problem 5 – Proposed Medium Rise Commercial Building
q: How many floors is the commercial building?
n: This is a bit tricky since the design problem did not actually mention the number of floors. However, it mentioned that the number of floors is the least number to be considered as a medium-rise building. We can refer to the glossary of the code to get the definition of a medium-rise building which is 6-15 storeys. Therefore, the building has 6 floors. The brief asks for the least number of storeys that still counts as medium-rise. Medium-rise is 6–15 storeys, so the answer is 6. Source: 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096 (NBCP), Glossary (Medium-Rise Building); HLURB Model Zoning Ordinance.

q: What is the difference in elevation between the sidewalk of the 15m RROW and the west side of the lot?
n: The lot is 40 m long on the 20 m road, and 1,600 sqm / 40 m = 40 m along the 15 m road. It falls 2% toward the west neighbor, so the difference is 40 m x 0.02 = 0.80 m, or 800 mm. Source: Brinker & Wolf, Elementary Surveying (Grades and Slopes).

q: Which is not an example of window opening treatments?
n: A light shelf is a daylighting device that reflects light deep into a room. Valances, shutters and drapes are window treatments. Source: Lechner, Heating, Cooling, Lighting (Light Shelves); Ching, Interior Design Illustrated.

q: Using a sanding sealer on wood is best if
n: Sanding sealer is used under clear (transparent) finishes like varnish and lacquer. It seals the wood and gives a smooth base without hiding the grain. Source: Fine Woodworking finishing references; Hoadley, Understanding Wood.

q: Aside from a structural engineer, who can interpret structural plans?
n: Architects are trained to read and coordinate structural plans with the architectural design. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 3 (Scope of Practice – coordination of allied works); Architect's Guidelines (2016).

q: A type of plywood that can be used for finishing due to its raw appearance.
n: Ribbon-grain (quarter-sliced) plywood has a decorative striped face veneer. It is used exposed as a finish surface. Source: Hardwood Plywood & Veneer Association (Veneer Cuts); Wood Handbook.

q: Aside from Romblon, where is another famous source of local marble?
n: Besides Romblon, Bulacan, in areas such as Doña Remedios Trinidad, is a known source of Philippine marble. Source: Mines and Geosciences Bureau (DENR), Philippine Mineral Resources – Marble.
